title: Free groups, 'no beer no music' bands, and his own band of 1918
summary: He lists the downtown and uptown groups he played with for free, then taking outside jobs, picture shows, and having his tunes written down.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

Susu Ramis played guitar Willie guitar played bass Harry Nunez played violin and I played the comic we played in the downtown section that is way down below Elysian Fields Avenue now this is 19 2 3 and 4 and 5 no night I made ahead I went ahead of my statement 19 3 4 and 5 and maybe 6 the uptown band I played with a boy named George Gieffer George Gieffer bass Joe Taranto guitar Freddie Inglot this boy sells ice cream around the streets today violin and Nick LaRocca this group this group and all the above groups was called no beer no music and when the refreshments ran out they all disappeared one by one in 1918 I formed my own band adding brass and clarinet I thinking I would get lots of jobs although I received a few people knew me wanted me to play for nothing as I had done before it was here that I started taking outside jobs I accepted jobs with Bill Gallaty that's a downtown group Dominic Baraka was a back of town group Joe Ella Bush was an Irish channel group in between times I played in picture shows I followed shows I hired myself out to play new music and it was here that I started putting these pieces together and having someone take them down in notation the original manuscripts I still have today and I have documents to prove not only from letters but from affidavits
